problem_type: new high-risk-path code (external data connector ingesting third-party scraped media) that could reintroduce four known risk classes: unbound IPC surface, plaintext BYO-key at rest, unrestricted outbound SSRF, and provenance loss on ingested media
symptom: This is a preventive structural contract for net-new code, not a corrective fix for an observed failure. The TikHub connector (v1) adds a code path where a user-supplied share link is resolved to a third-party media URL and the bytes are ingested into a project. Several touched files sit on high-risk prefixes/patterns (electron/catalog/ for the credential store, electron/assets/ for the media store, an electron *Ipc.ts registration, and — with v1.1 — a new *store.ts connector-prefs persistence file), so without an explicit boundary the change could silently (a) register an unguarded IPC channel, (b) persist the BYO API key as plaintext, (c) fetch an attacker-influenced URL without SSRF/allowlist protection, or (d) land scraped media with no source evidence so it is later treated as commercially usable. The v1.1 dual-domain globalization widens the outbound surface: the connector now reaches TikHub over two candidate hosts (api.tikhub.io primary + api.tikhub.dev mainland-China accelerator) with a measured route race, sticky selection, and automatic failover. This adds two new obligations of the SAME classes: (e) every new health probe AND the failover-retried request must go through the SAME hardenedFetch boundary under an allowlist that now covers BOTH hosts (never a bare fetch to the picked host, and the probe must never carry the Authorization/BYO key so it stays free and unauthenticated), and (f) the sticky route preference must persist as a NON-credential value in a plain connector-prefs store — never the credential store — and the resolved host is hard-checked to be one of the two candidates so a poisoned preference can never redirect outbound traffic off-allowlist.
direct_cause: Introducing a data connector requires new surface in exactly the places the ratchet marks high-risk: a preload/main IPC pair (tikhubConnectorIpc.ts), reuse of the credential-at-rest store (secrets.ts / apiKeysByVendor), an outbound HTTP client, and a write into projectAssetStore. Each of these is an entry point for a class of regression the codebase already guards elsewhere; the connector must route through the existing shared boundaries rather than open a parallel unprotected path.
class_root: External-source ingestion is a class, not a one-off: any connector that turns a user/agent-supplied reference into fetched bytes has the same four obligations (sender-bound IPC, encrypted-only credential write, hardenedFetch+origin allowlist for every outbound call, and AssetSourceEvidence with rightsStatus:'unknown' for every landed media). The failure mode of doing it per-connector is that one connector forgets one obligation and reintroduces a plaintext key, an SSRF hole, or unattributed media. The remedy is to make each obligation a single shared boundary that every ingestion path is forced through, and to prove the new connector routes through them.
affected_population: Every user who configures the TikHub connector and pastes a Douyin/TikTok share link: their BYO key must never land as plaintext, and the resolved third-party URL must be fetched only under SSRF/allowlist protection
Every project video asset ingested via a connector: it must carry AssetSourceEvidence with rightsStatus:'unknown' so downstream delivery never infers it is licensed for commercial use
Any future data connector added on the same high-risk paths: it inherits the identical four obligations and must reuse these boundaries rather than open a parallel unprotected path
entry_points: registerTikhubConnectorIpc (electron/connectors/tikhubConnectorIpc.ts) — the seven IPC handlers (key-status/save-key/clear-key/route-status/set-route/resolve-share-url/import-to-project); every one calls assertTrustedSender before touching credentials, preferences, or the network

fetchTikhubJson (electron/connectors/tikhubConnector.ts) — the resolve/import outbound path; goes through hardenedFetch with a hard allowlist check that the resolved host is one of the two candidates (api.tikhub.io | api.tikhub.dev), redirects disabled, Authorization declared sensitive

probeTikhubHost (electron/connectors/tikhubRoute.ts) — the route-race health probe (GET /api/v1/health/check per host); goes through the SAME hardenedFetch boundary, carries NO Authorization (free/unauthenticated, so it can never bill or leak the key), redirects disabled

resolveTikhubHost / failoverTikhubHost (electron/connectors/tikhubRoute.ts) — pick/switch the outbound host; only ever return a host from the TIKHUB_HOSTS candidate list, and persist the sticky choice via the connector-prefs store, never the credential store

readConnectorPrefs / writeConnectorPrefs (electron/connectors/connectorPrefsStore.ts) — the non-credential connector-preferences store; holds only the route mode + sticky host (both normalized against the candidate list), never any secret; the BYO key stays exclusively in the safeStorage credential store
saveTikhubApiKey (electron/connectors/tikhubConnectorService.ts) — writes the BYO key only via the catalog credential upsert, which is safeStorage-encrypted and fail-closed; no plaintext side path
importTikhubShareUrl → importRemoteAsset (electron/assets/projectAssetStore.ts) — lands the resolved media with a sanitized AssetSourceEvidence pinned to rightsStatus:'unknown'

external_sources.purpose: Reconcile the exact endpoints, query params, auth scheme, and response envelope this connector exposes. Confirmed Authorization: Bearer {token}; ResponseModel envelope {code,message,message_zh,request_id,data} with data typed anyOf:[{},null] (untyped platform passthrough); the only OpenAPI-documented clean direct-URL field is data.original_video_url on fetch_video_high_quality_play_url (per its endpoint description, $0.005/call).

invariants: Every connector IPC handler binds its sender: no registration reaches credentials, preferences, or the network without assertTrustedSender (held by check:ipc-sender-binding).

The connector's BYO key is written only through the catalog credential store, which is safeStorage-encrypted and fail-closed; no code path persists the key as plaintext, and the non-credential connector-prefs store never holds any secret (only route mode + sticky host).

Every outbound connector request — the resolve/import calls AND the route-race health probes — goes through hardenedFetch with an origin allowlist covering BOTH candidate hosts (api.tikhub.io | api.tikhub.dev) and redirects disabled; there is no bare fetch. The Authorization header is declared sensitive on the resolve/import calls (stripped on cross-origin redirects), and the free health probe carries NO Authorization at all.

The outbound host is always one of the two TIKHUB_HOSTS candidates: resolveTikhubHost/failoverTikhubHost only ever return a candidate host, the sticky preference is normalized against the candidate list on read, and fetchTikhubJson hard-rejects any host outside it — so a poisoned connector-prefs value can never redirect traffic off-allowlist.

Every media landed through importRemoteAsset from a connector carries AssetSourceEvidence sanitized to source='connector' with rightsStatus pinned to 'unknown'; commercial usability is never inferred from scraped provenance.
generality_proof: The four invariants are enforced by shared boundaries that all ingestion paths pass through, not by connector-local checks. sanitizeSourceEvidence in projectAssetStore.ts is the single write choke point that pins rightsStatus:'unknown' for any caller supplying source evidence (browser capture, future connectors, and TikHub alike); it whitelists fields so an untrusted payload cannot smuggle a different rightsStatus. The credential write goes through the same applyApiKeyUpsert path as every vendor key (safeStorage-only, fail-closed, non-header-safe-char guarded). Outbound goes through hardenedFetch, the same SSRF/DoS boundary importRemoteAsset and extractVideoFrame already use. IPC binding is enforced generically by check:ipc-sender-binding over all electron *Ipc.ts registrations. A second connector added tomorrow inherits all four without new per-connector code.

shared_boundaries.responsibility: Single write choke point that normalizes any caller-supplied source evidence into the connector provenance shape and pins rightsStatus:'unknown'; whitelists fields so no untrusted payload can assert a different rights status or smuggle arbitrary metadata into the asset sidecar. Every media landed via importRemoteAsset (browser capture, TikHub, any future connector) passes through it.

same_class_entry_points.evidence: Both the http and data-url branches thread the sanitized sourceEvidence into writeAsset metadata; sanitizeSourceEvidence hard-pins rightsStatus:'unknown' and whitelists fields. projectAssetStore.sourceEvidence.test.ts asserts a payload claiming rightsStatus:'commercial' is coerced to 'unknown' and unknown fields are dropped.

The resolve/import outbound path hard-checks that url.hostname is one of the two TIKHUB_HOSTS candidates (api.tikhub.io | api.tikhub.dev), disables redirects, and declares Authorization sensitive. tikhubTransport.test.ts pins the Bearer header, sensitiveHeaders, allowRedirect:false, throwOnNon2xx:false, and the status→kind error classification (with the route layer stubbed to a fixed host so this suite isolates the outbound contract).

The route-race health probe goes through the SAME hardenedFetch boundary (GET /api/v1/health/check), carries NO Authorization header (free/unauthenticated), and disables redirects; the resolved/failover host is always a TIKHUB_HOSTS candidate and the sticky choice is normalized against that list on read. tikhubRoute.test.ts pins: the probe URL + absence of Authorization + allowRedirect:false, the locale-only ordering, the race-then-sticky write, primary-down→next-host, both-down→null, manual io/dev forcing (no probe), failover to the alternate, and mode persistence clearing sticky on return to auto.

A plain settings-root JSON store partitioned by connectorId that holds only non-secret preferences (route mode + sticky host). The BYO key never touches it — it stays exclusively in the safeStorage credential store via applyApiKeyUpsert. tikhubRoute.test.ts drives it through an in-memory fake and asserts only route mode + candidate-list-normalized host are ever written.

All seven handlers (key-status/save-key/clear-key/route-status/set-route/resolve-share-url/import-to-project) call assertTrustedSender before importing the service; check:ipc-sender-binding scans every electron *Ipc.ts registration and reports 0 new unguarded (the new handlers are guarded, so they never enter the unguarded baseline).

prevention.invariant: Any media ingested through importRemoteAsset with source evidence lands with rightsStatus pinned to 'unknown'; the rights status can never be raised by a caller-supplied payload.
prevention.failure_mode: Without the single sanitizer, a connector (or a compromised renderer payload) could attach source evidence asserting rightsStatus:'commercial' or 'licensed', and scraped third-party media would later be treated as safe for commercial delivery.
prevention.strategy: Route all source-evidence attachment through one sanitizeSourceEvidence choke point in projectAssetStore that whitelists fields and hard-codes rightsStatus:'unknown', so every current and future ingestion path is forced through it rather than writing evidence directly.

recurrence.reason: External-source ingestion is a recurring class: every data connector that turns a user/agent-supplied reference into fetched bytes carries the same obligations, and dual-domain reach adds one more instance of the outbound obligation (health probes + failover retries) plus a non-credential-persistence obligation. Rather than re-checking them per connector or per host, the change routes each obligation through an existing shared boundary (sanitizeSourceEvidence for provenance, applyApiKeyUpsert for credentials, hardenedFetch for ALL outbound — resolve/import AND probes — assertTrustedSender for IPC) and keeps the sticky route in a separate non-secret store, then proves the TikHub connector goes through them.
same_class_scan: Enumerated every path that lands remote media into a project via importRemoteAsset: browser capture / browser-upload, generation outputs, decomposeLayers, and now the TikHub connector — all now pass through the single sanitizeSourceEvidence choke point when they supply source evidence, and none writes rightsStatus directly.

Enumerated every BYO-credential write: all vendor keys and the TikHub connector key go through applyApiKeyUpsert (safeStorage-only, fail-closed, non-header-safe-char guarded); confirmed the new connector-prefs store (connectorPrefsStore.ts) holds ONLY non-secret preferences (route mode + sticky host) and never the key; secrets.ts still only re-exports the status type owner and the encrypt/decrypt primitives are unchanged.

Enumerated every connector outbound call: fetchTikhubJson (resolve/import) AND probeTikhubHost (route race) — both go through hardenedFetch, now with an allowlist covering BOTH candidate hosts (api.tikhub.io | api.tikhub.dev) and redirects disabled; the probe carries no Authorization, and the resolved/failover host is always a candidate (normalized on read, hard-checked before fetch) so a poisoned sticky value cannot go off-allowlist. Same SSRF/DoS boundary importRemoteAsset and extractVideoFrame already use; grepped the connectors directory for bare fetch( and found none.

Enumerated every electron *Ipc.ts registration via check:ipc-sender-binding: the seven TikHub handlers (including the two new route-status/set-route) all call assertTrustedSender and therefore never enter the unguarded baseline, which stays at its prior count.

legacy_paths.rationale: This is net-new connector code with no prior implementation to remove; there is no parallel or legacy ingestion path being replaced. secrets.ts changes only relocate the ApiKeyDecryptStatus owner to the neutral contract layer and re-export it, leaving all existing import sites and behavior intact.

dependency_lifecycle.rationale: No third-party dependency is added, upgraded, or retained by this change. TikHub is reached over plain HTTPS through the existing hardenedFetch client; there is no SDK or new package.

migration: No stored data is rewritten and no existing behavior changes. secrets.ts relocates the ApiKeyDecryptStatus members to electron/shared/contracts/apiKeyStatus.ts and re-exports the type so every existing import path keeps working unchanged. projectAssetStore gains a sourceEvidence passthrough that is inert unless a caller supplies connector source evidence, so all prior importRemoteAsset callers are unaffected. The TikHub key rides the same apiKeysByVendor safeStorage store as every vendor key with no schema change.
residual_risks: TikHub is a third-party scraping API (not official platform access). Resolved direct URLs are short-lived and can break as platform anti-bot measures change; the connector surfaces this honestly in its failure messages but cannot prevent upstream fluctuation.

The OpenAPI types ResponseModel.data as an untyped passthrough, so the aweme play-URL field paths for fetch_one_video_by_share_url are not machine-documented; the parser walks defensive candidate paths and the fixtures are synthetic, to be confirmed by the gated TIKHUB_E2E=1 smoke against a real key after delivery.

rightsStatus is pinned to 'unknown', which is correct but conservative: legitimately reusable content is also marked unknown, so downstream commercial-use gating must treat 'unknown' as 'do not assume licensed' rather than blocking outright.
